newsitem.title: THAILAND: Iran negotiating 400,000T Thai rice deal. [CORRECTED 12:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iran negotiating 400,000T Thai rice deal. [CORRECTED 12:27 GMT]

text.p: Iran is seeking to buy 400,000 tonnes of rice form Thailand but a deal has not been concluded yet, Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said on Monday.

He told reporters after meeting the Iranian ambassador to Thailand that Teheran had asked the government to help negotiate with exporters as most of them were reluctant to accept the proposed price and stringent Iranian terms.
Under its tough terms, Iran required that the purchased rice must be inspected by its officials and that the sacks the rice was packed in should be thicker than normal.
"The price of Thai rice remains high even though the second crop rice supplies are entering the market. Iran found the price too high and asked whether we could lower it a bit," Narongchai said.
"Moreover, it is very unlikely (corrects from "likely") that the exporters will accept the Iranian terms. But we will help in the negotiation," he added

According to the Rice Policy Committee's resolution, Thailand should sell rice to Iran on a cash basis only and not on credit as Iran had not met all its debt obligation from previous purchase. No details about Iran's previous debt was available.
